challenges.says: Step 3 claims to keep the comment-first rule (businessrule-78566706966921753288) and the refresh-either-way rule (businessrule-70167687024707690035) but never says a comment is stored first, nor that the view refreshes after success or partial failure.
This journey is today's Verify then Apply flow in new words; the only difference is the merged file/reset step, so it adds little as the task-first variant.
The recommendation says text can never be applied unchecked, but Apply already refuses unreadable text (businessrule-30078789996227150580); the claimed benefit is not new.

Step 1 honours businessrule-27078270365699057081, where Open File replaces the text 'without asking and without checking it', yet it now checks on arrival; it also drops the confirmed Reset (start again) from the intent and system, though block-20479299247601531941 is cited as merged in.
Reading on arrival leaves unclear when typed or edited text is re-checked, since the step covers only 'a file or entered'; a person who edits the text after the check can see a stale count or fault.

The step claims 'reading is possible but not required', but the system only provides the text to take and the person can no longer see what is being copied, which loses the read step and the focus-and-select behaviour (block-18241451168755948032).

Step 2 changes rule businessrule-62209428351075007862 (a hidden policy leaves nothing happening and no message) and businessrule-73292110340688125936 (the area is the lower of the area shown and the area found) into 'tells the person when hidden' and 'computer in preference to user', yet marks both as kept.

Step 1 does not mention the area choice (businessrule-81666786810242280110) or the stale-section behaviour (businessrule-56645748073860464161), and it honours businessrule-75178338270301910966, which is about the edit dialog refreshing and not about going to an identifier.

Step 2 repeats details that step 1 already opens for a product or support definition (businessrule-49582367227471127226), and its claim that details are 'not a dialog every time' is not a change, because today only products and support definitions open one.

Step 1 lists businessrule-63262725504588029346 as kept and honoured, but that rule is a silent drop of an unclosed quote, while the system now tells the person; the contradiction is not named as a change, and the single-quote absorbing behaviour is not addressed.

Searching on every change contradicts the rule that Search is pressed to refuse empty text (businessrule-73561308167207352856): there is no press, and the person would see 'words are needed' constantly while typing the first character.
